name: Centennial
chain: Roadway Design & Construction Standards Manual (2024 ed. of 2016-08-17 adoption)
Gap-fill: AASHTO Green Book, CDOT Standard Specs, MUTCD, MGPEC (always latest editions)

geometry.note: Genuine SILENT on geometry, verified by full reads: taper lengths per MUTCD §6C.08 (2009 numbering — section content moved in the 11th Ed; Designated Rep may adjust); no city tables; Appendix A Standard Details (2024) contains no TC series (checked, not assumed).

deltas.rule: Arrow panels required on arterial maintenance work; short-term stationary (>1 hr, one day) and short-duration (<=1 hr) work requires a rotating beacon/strobe (arrow board/stick substitutable).
deltas.baseline: arrow panel optional per MUTCD for many maintenance operations

source.doc: Centennial Roadway Design & Construction Standards Manual

deltas.rule: All excavations: safety orange fence + Type 1 barriers with reflective lights.

effect.note: plus safety orange fence, with reflective lights

deltas.rule: Cones are daytime-only; lighted barricades overnight — steady burn = delineation, flashing = hazard (near-verbatim Littleton LEDS §131 text; but AFAD rule diverges — see devices).

source.doc: Centennial Roadway Design & Construction Standards Manual

deltas.rule: Steel plates not permitted unless specifically authorized by the Designated Rep; temporary cold-mix (or HMA) surface required at the end of EACH workday; millings/aggregates banned. No seasonal rule — discretionary-plus-daily-surface posture.

source.doc: Centennial Roadway Design & Construction Standards Manual

deltas.rule: Pedestrians never diverted onto the roadway (accessible detour unless the City waives); open trenches prohibited after work hours without approval; no construction until all TC devices are in place per the approved TCP.
TC setup and removal must occur within work hours unless the TCP says otherwise (prep that doesn't interfere is allowed).

windows.note: Permitted night work on arterials/collectors 7 p.m.-5 a.m. (continues 0:00-5:00 next day).

hours.override_note: No Saturday/Sunday/Holiday work without Designated Representative approval. Out-of-hours lane closures need written approval; violations -> Notice of Violation.

personnel.rule: Major TC: TCP shall be prepared by an ATSSA Certified Traffic Control Supervisor when ANY of: zone passes through an intersection · work within an intersection · full street closures · detours · when required by the City Traffic Engineer. (Authorship gate, not on-site-presence.)

trigger.condition: work in/through an intersection, or City Traffic Engineer requires

personnel.rule: 'When the normal operation of a traffic signal must be interrupted, uniformed officers SHALL be used to direct traffic. This shall be coordinated with the City and Arapahoe County Sheriff's Office prior to the work. The Contractor shall bear any expense.'

source.doc: Centennial Roadway Design & Construction Standards Manual

personnel.rule: Flaggers per MUTCD procedures; ANSI Class 2 apparel (day) / Class 3 (night) — first explicit ANSI class spec in the corpus. No flagger-certification requirement stated (vs. Littleton's CDOT-cert rule).

source.doc: Centennial Roadway Design & Construction Standards Manual

devices.rule: Maintenance TC (MUTCD 6G classes): >=5 cones from the vehicle rear, spaced = speed limit (ft), per adjacent lane. Mobile ops: TA-35 (>2 lanes) / TA-17 (2 lanes), shadow vehicles with arrow panels; cones/attenuators not required.

VMS may be required on arterials, placed >=48 hrs ahead. AFADs may be used at the discretion of the PW Director/designee in coordination with the City Traffic Engineer (opposite of Littleton's ban, in otherwise-copied text).

source.doc: Centennial Roadway Design & Construction Standards Manual

tiers.label: Minor TC
tiers.definition: MUTCD Typical Application plans 'may be copied and submitted as traffic control plans' — enumerated TA 1, 3, 4, 6, 15, 16, 17, 18, 21-29 (TA numbering survives the 11th Ed intact; cite TAs by number, never by figure). Comply with the TA submitted; separate TCP where TAs don't fit; sidewalk closures always need a TCP.

tiers.label: Major TC
tiers.definition: TCP authored by an ATSSA Certified TCS (triggers in personnel).

notes.rule: Review identity: City of Centennial / 'Public Works Director or designee' (the review, permit, NOV, and field-modification authority). No contract operator appears in any public document.

Bond: $20,000 minimum for the permit term; Excepted Entities (gov agencies, utilities, water/san districts) may substitute a Letter of Responsibility and Agreement to Perform naming the City beneficiary.

Application requires estimated quantities (fees computed from them); amendment mandatory when any permitted quantity grows >10%; extensions by written request >=10 working days pre-expiry, minimum fee = base fee. Punchlist + final inspection within 7 calendar days.
Pavement restoration fee is OCI-based — charged when the permit holder elects NOT to do the required 2" mill-and-overlay (length of cut x full lane width); OCI reset each Jan 1.

multi_agency.rule: GESC permits (standard and low-impact) are issued DIRECTLY through SEMSWA — an external authority issuing permits inside the city; SEMSWA approvals gate City permits (culverts/chase drains, SEMSWA-first). Signal interruptions coordinate with the Arapahoe County Sheriff's Office. MGPEC standards apply.

fees.note: Fee amounts live on a separate Fee Schedule (counters at both facilities, or website) — not yet captured (Q-CEN-3). Refunds restricted; admin fee on cancellations.

leads.label: Permit processing
leads.note: Up to 14 calendar days from accepted application.

leads.label: Completion inspection before leaving the site
leads.note: Scheduled >=24 hrs before leaving; leaving without it is an NOV.

leads.label: Emergency permit
leads.note: Call 303-325-8000 first; permit within 2 business days; pickup within 5 working days.

source.doc: Centennial Roadway Design & Construction Standards Manual

notices.rule: Door hangers/flyers >=48 hrs when required; news releases + HOA meetings may be required; signal/loop damage reported immediately to 303-325-8000.

items.rule: Signed TCP kept at the work area, available to City or State inspection (Manual §6.6.4 #14).

source.doc: Centennial Roadway Design & Construction Standards Manual
